question: In which patient would an urgent coronary angiography be performed?

options.opa: 66-year-old diabetic woman with a single episode of pain at rest and elevation of troponins.
options.opb: A 77-year-old man admitted for two 30-minute episodes of pain with a decrease in the ST segment on the ECG during the episode of pain.
options.opc: A 55-year-old man who, after a week of treatment with double antiaggregation, underwent an isotopic ergometry showing extensive ischemia in the anterior face.
options.opd: A 65-year-old woman with pain at rest and positive clinical ergometry in the third stage of Bruce.
options.ope: A 55-year-old patient admitted for chest pain and dyspnea saturating 80% despite the administration of oxygen and with an ECG with ST-segment depression in the anterolateral aspect that does not revert with the administration of intravenous nitroglycerin.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: 66-year-old diabetic woman -> single episode of pain at rest -> elevation of troponins -> urgent coronary angiography -> 95% confidence CHAIN: 77-year-old man -> two 30-minute episodes of pain -> decrease in ST segment on ECG -> urgent coronary angiography -> 90% confidence CHAIN: 55-year-old man -> week of treatment with double antiaggregation -> isotopic ergometry showing extensive ischemia -> urgent coronary angiography -> 85% confidence CHAIN: 65-year-old woman -> pain at rest -> positive clinical ergometry in third stage of Bruce -> urgent coronary angiography -> 80% confidence CHAIN: 55-year-old patient -> chest pain and dyspnea saturating -> 95%
analysis: Urgent coronary angiography is indicated in patients with ongoing chest pain at rest despite medical therapy, evidence of myocardial ischemia on ECG, or elevated troponins. The patient in option e fits these criteria.
